entities.summary:
Falco of Maastricht was a bishop of Maastricht from 495 until 512, venerated as a Roman Catholic saint.

 He was born unknown and died on December 12, 512 CE.

 Falco of Maastricht played a significant role in the Catholic Church, serving as bishop during a time of great religious change.

 His legacy can be seen in the many churches and cathedrals he built, including the famous St. Servatius Church in Maastricht.

 The city of Maastricht still celebrates Falco of Maastricht as a patron saint, with annual festivities and cultural events.

 "May the light of Christ illuminate our path," Falco of Maastricht once said, inspiring generations of Catholics.

 Falco of Maastricht's impact extends beyond the Netherlands, with his legacy influencing Catholicism throughout Europe.

 Falco of Maastricht's contributions to the Catholic Church cannot be overstated, cementing his place in history as a devoted servant of the faith.
